claims.claim_vi: The source covers vertical partitioning, horizontal partitioning (sharding), a routing algorithm, range-based and hash-based sharding, benefits and drawbacks.
claims.verified_by: Source body read at the pinned commit; only the names are used.

claims.claim_vi: Changing the shard count under hash mod N moves most keys: 100000 integer keys 0..99999 hashed with MD5 move 80.0% from mod 4 to mod 5, 49.9% from 4 to 8, 90.9% from 10 to 11; a consistent-hash ring (MD5 as a 128-bit integer; key hashed from its decimal string; shard j point i hashed from the string 'j-i', 200 points per shard; first point at or after the key hash, wrapping) moved 19.9% of the 100000 keys when a fifth shard was added to four.
claims.verified_by: Computed by the author in the writing session with Python (hashlib.md5); the code is not stored, the method is written in the lesson.

claims.claim_vi: Range sharding keeps range queries on few shards but concentrates monotonically increasing keys on one shard; hash sharding spreads data but needs every shard for range queries.
claims.verified_by: General knowledge of the author, not checked against an official document: the writing environment could only reach GitHub, and no official document for this topic is hosted there.

design_notes_vi: Khung một có hai thẻ cắt theo cột và theo hàng; khung hai là bốn ghi chú về chia theo khoảng và theo băm.
source_deviations: Source lists benefits and drawbacks; the lesson attaches the trade-off to each item and adds a measured experiment on changing the shard count.
The lesson states that vertical partitioning here means cutting columns, not a bigger machine.
